problem:
$\,$ $x$ is a member of the set of integer numbers.

The predicate $P(x)$ is given above. Which of following represents $¬P(x)?$

choices.value: $x$ is a member of the set of integer numbers
$x$ is a member of the set of real numbers
$x$ is not a member of the set of integer numbers
$x$ is not a member of the set of real numbers
$x$ is not a member of the set of rational numbers

feedback.problem:
Given that 

$$
P(x):x\text{ is }\text{not}\text{ greater than }7,
$$

 
which of the following represents $¬P(x)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The symbol "$¬$" represents negation. So, our task is to negate the given sentence. 

To negate our plain English sentence, we place the words "It is not true that" in front of it. This gives the following:

$$
¬P(x):\text{It is not true that }x\text{ is }\text{not}\text{ greater than }7,
$$

 

In other words, $x$ is greater than $7.$ Therefore, $¬P(x)$ means the following:

$$
¬P(x):x\text{ is greater than }7.
$$
